record.title: Authors report that gradient-guided fine-tuning data filtering reduces jailbreak success across three model families
record.summary: A new preprint presents SimpleLoRIF, a gradient-embedding method for locating benign-looking fine-tuning examples associated with unsafe behavior. The authors report that removing the 20% of Tulu 3 examples most aligned with unsafe responses reduced GCG attack success across Qwen, Llama and Olmo, while largely preserving selected capability scores. These are bounded author-reported results; the paper tests one target set and general safety, and independent reproduction remains open.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The authors submitted version 1 of “Follow the Gradient: Tracing Safety Degradation Back to Training Data” to arXiv on October 27, 2026.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that removing the 20% of Tulu 3 examples with the greatest gradient similarity to unsafe SafeRLHF responses reduced GCG attack success from 47.7% to 37.0% for Qwen 3 1.7B, from 38.0% to 30.3% for Llama 3.2 1B, and from 48.3% to 41.0% for Olmo 2 1B. They report three fine-tuning seeds and standard errors; capability results were largely preserved or improved on the selected benchmarks.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that gradients from insecure-code fine-tuning examples aligned with harmful behaviors after fine-tuning, with AUC 0.865 for one Mistral model and 0.604 for one Qwen model.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The preprint does not establish independent reproduction, effectiveness on other target sets or specific behaviors such as sycophancy, or improved safety in production deployment.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent group reproduced the gradient-attribution or SafeTulu fine-tuning results in this activation.
The authors state they test general safety, not specific behaviors such as sycophancy, and use one unsafe-response target set.
Code, dataset and exact scoring artifacts were not audited or executed in this activation.

brief.importance_rationale: If reproduced beyond this regime, identifying benign-looking fine-tuning examples associated with broad harmful behavior and reducing attack success through data filtering could materially change post-training safety practice. The present evidence is author-reported and bounded to selected small models and evaluations.
limitations: All outcome measurements are reported by the paper authors and remain unconfirmed by independent reproduction.
Reported filtering results cover three small models, selected attack and capability benchmarks, and one unsafe-response target set.
The paper does not test specific safety behaviors such as sycophancy.
brief.summary: A new preprint presents SimpleLoRIF, a gradient-embedding method for locating benign-looking fine-tuning examples associated with unsafe behavior. The authors report that removing the 20% of Tulu 3 examples most aligned with unsafe responses reduced GCG attack success across Qwen, Llama and Olmo, while largely preserving selected capability scores. These are bounded author-reported results; the paper tests one target set and general safety, and independent reproduction remains open.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report that SimpleLoRIF ranks benign-looking instruction examples by gradient alignment to unsafe responses; removing the highest-scoring 20% of Tulu 3 reduces GCG attack success across Qwen, Llama and Olmo while preserving selected capability benchmarks.
technical.demonstrated_result: The full primary preprint and its reported methods, tables, limitations and reproducibility statement were inspected. Code was not run and the results were not independently reproduced.
technical.mechanism: SimpleLoRIF computes compact gradient embeddings by restricting backpropagation to the final four transformer blocks. The authors score each Tulu 3 example against clustered gradients from 43,469 unsafe-response examples in SafeRLHF, remove the 20% highest-similarity examples, then fine-tune and evaluate models.
technical.regime: Authors use Qwen 3 0.6B embeddings and fine-tune Qwen 3 1.7B, Llama 3.2 1B and Olmo 2 1B on Tulu 3. They report three seeds and evaluate GCG, ActorBreaker and selected capability/over-refusal benchmarks. SafeTulu removes 20% of the examples.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper compares against baseline training, random removal, LLM-as-a-judge filtering and a prior gradient-based filtering method. Reported GCG success decreases by 10.7, 7.7 and 7.3 percentage points for Qwen, Llama and Olmo respectively.

brief.title: Authors report that gradient-guided fine-tuning data filtering reduces jailbreak success across three model families
brief.why_it_matters: The work proposes a way to find safety-degrading signals that ordinary text filters may miss, linking model behavior to fine-tuning examples and turning that signal into a data-filtering intervention. If the reported effects reproduce across target sets, model scales and behavior-specific evaluations, this could inform post-training data curation; current results do not establish general safety or production impact.
